transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I suppose it’s the tension, really. My neck and shoulders… and even my jaw, they’re tight most of the time now. It feels like I’m sort of bracing for something, even when I’m just at my desk or watching TV.
Do you notice that the tension in your neck, shoulders, or jaw gets worse during times of stress or worry?

Yes… it does seem worse when I’m worried. But honestly, it’s there a lot of the time now—my neck and shoulders, and my jaw too. Like I’m bracing myself, even if I’m only sitting at my desk or watching TV.
Do you find it hard to relax or feel restless, even when there’s no obvious reason to be worried?

Yes… I suppose I do. I feel sort of wound up most of the day, like I’m waiting for the next thing to go wrong. At school I catch myself pacing around the classroom, or checking my phone between periods for messages from the contractor. It’s hard to just sit and switch off.
Have you noticed any other physical symptoms like headaches, fatigue, or trouble sleeping that seem related to this constant tension and worry?

Yes… fatigue, mostly. By the end of the school day, when the last bell goes, I feel completely wrung out. It’s not really fixed by a decent night’s sleep or a quiet Sunday. Even marking a small pile of quizzes can feel like… pushing through mud.
Do you notice any other areas of your body that feel tense or uncomfortable, like your back, chest, or stomach, even when you’re not doing anything physically demanding?
Mostly it’s my neck, shoulders, and jaw. They’re tight almost all the time now… like I’m bracing myself for something bad, even if I’m just sitting at my desk or watching TV.
Do you feel like your worry is something you can’t control or that it takes over your thoughts even when you try to focus on something else?

Yes… I think so. I can tell myself to stop and pay attention to the class in front of me, but then one small thing comes up — a late invoice, or a student who’s slipping behind — and it turns into a whole string of what-ifs. I don’t seem to be able to shut it off very well.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about a variety of things, even when the situation doesn’t seem like a big deal to others?

Yes… it does jump around a lot. It can be something small, like wondering if the contractors missed something in the house, and then I’m off thinking about lesson plans, or whether the robotics students are falling behind.

And then it sort of turns into… whether I’m letting my wife or family down by not keeping everything under control. Other people might not see those things as big, but they don’t feel small in my head.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because your mind is racing or you're worrying, even when you're physically tired?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I do get tired, but I haven’t paid much attention to whether it’s the worrying keeping me up. Sleep hasn’t been something I’ve thought about in that much detail.
Do you notice any other areas of your body that feel tense or uncomfortable, like your back, chest, or stomach, even when you’re not doing anything physically demanding?
Yes… mostly my neck and shoulders. My jaw too, actually. They’re tight a lot of the time now, even if I’m just sitting at my desk or watching TV. It feels like I’m sort of bracing myself, I guess.
Do you notice any other parts of your body, like your chest, stomach, or back, feeling tense or uncomfortable even when you're not doing anything physically strenuous?
Mostly the same places I mentioned… my neck, shoulders, and jaw. It’s pretty constant lately, like I’m tensed up waiting for something bad, even if I’m just sitting at my desk or watching TV.
Do you ever feel tension or discomfort in other parts of your body, like your chest, stomach, or back, even when you’re not doing anything physically strenuous?

Not really chest or stomach so much. It’s more… like I said, my neck and shoulders, and my jaw. They’re tight almost all the time now, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or watching TV. It feels like I’m bracing for bad news or something.
Do you find it difficult to relax, even in situations where there’s no immediate stress or pressure?

Yeah… I do. Even when nothing’s happening, I feel sort of wound up most of the day. Like I’m waiting for the next thing to go wrong. I’ll catch myself pacing around the classroom between periods, or checking my phone for messages from the contractor. It’s hard to just… settle.
Do you find yourself worrying about a number of different things, such as work responsibilities, family matters, and everyday tasks, even when others might not see them as urgent or important?

Yeah… I suppose so. It jumps around a lot. One minute I’m thinking the contractors must’ve missed something with the house, then it’s whether my lesson plans are falling behind, or the robotics students aren’t where they should be. And then I start thinking I’m letting my wife or the family down because I can’t keep everything under control.
How long have you been feeling this way — constantly worried and physically tense — has it been going on for months, or did it start more recently in response to a specific situation?
It’s been months, yeah. I’d say about seven months… since the pipe burst and the remodeling started. That’s when the house sort of got turned upside down, and I haven’t really settled since.
Do you notice any other parts of your body, like your chest, stomach, or back, feeling tense or uncomfortable even when you're not doing anything physically strenuous?

Yeah… mostly my neck and shoulders. My jaw too, actually. They’re tight a lot of the time now, even if I’m just sitting at my desk or trying to watch TV. It feels like I’m sort of bracing myself all the time.
